FOREWORD 

This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the 
Geotextiles Sectional Committee had been approved by the Textile Division CouncjL 

Using a geotextile as a medium to retain soil particles necessitates compatibility between it and the 
adjacent soil. This test method is used to indicate the apparent opening size of a geotextile, which reflects 
the approximate largest opening dimension available for soil to pass through. 

In the preparation of this standard assistance has been drawn from ASTM Designation : E4751-87 
'Standard lest method for determining apparent opcnmg size of a geotextile', issued by the American 
Society for Testing and Materials, USA. 

In reporting the results of a lest or analysis made in accordance with this standard, if ihe final value, 
observed or calculated, is to be rounded off, it shall be done in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 'Rules for 
rounding oif numerical values {revised)\

IS 14294 : 1995 



Indian Standard 

GEOTEXTILES — METHOD FOR 

DETERMINATION OF APPARENT 

OPENING SIZE BY DRY SIEVING 

TECHNIQUE 



1 SCOPE 

This Indjan Standard specifies method lo deter- 
mine apparent opening size (AGS) by sieving glass 
beads through the geoiextile. This method is 
suitable for AOS 60 microns and above, 

2 REFERENCES 

The following Indian Standards are necessary ad- 
juncts to this standard: 

IS No. Tale 

460 Specification for test sieves : 

(Part 1) : 1985 Part 1 Wire cloth test sieves (thud 
revision) (Reaffirmed 1990) 

(Part 2) ; 1985 Part 2 Perforated plate test sieves 
(third revision) (Reaffirmed 
1990) 

(Part 3) ' 1985 Part 3 Methods of examination of 
apertures of test sieves (third 
revision) (Reaffirmed 1990) 

6359 : 1971 Method for conditioning of tex- 

tiles (Reaffirmed 1993) 

13321 Glossary of terms for geosyn- 

(Partl):1992 thetics: Part 1 Terms used in 
materials and properties. 

3 TERMINOLOGY 

For the purpose of this standard dcfinuions as 
given in IS 13321 (Part 1) : 1992 shall apply. 

4 PRINCIPLE 

A specimen of geotextile is placed in a sieve frame 
and sized glass beads are placed on the geotextile 
surface. The geotextile and frame are shaken 
laterally so that the jarring motion will induce the 
beads to pass through the lest specimen. The pro- 
cedure is repeated on the same specimen wuh 
various size glass beads until its apparent opening 
size has been determined. 

5 APPARATUS 

5,1 Mechanical Sieve Shaker — A mechanical 
sieve shaker, if used, shall impart a vertical, or 



lateral and vertical, motion to the sieve, causing the 
particles thereon to bounce and return so as to 
present different orientations to the sievmgsur- 
face. 

5.2 Pan, Cover and 200 mm Diameter Sieves 

5.3 Spherical Glass Beads, in size fractions in ac- 
cordance with Table 1. It is only necessary to have 
on hand the bead size fractions necessary for the 
range of gcotextiles for which testing is anticipated. 
The sizing of all beads shall be verified prior to each 
use by sievmg on the pairs of selves shown in 
Table I. Prepare at least 50 g of each size fraction 
to be used prior to beginning the test. 

5.4 Balance, having a capacity adequate for the 
mass of samples anticipated and accurate to 
±0.05 g. 

5.5 Static Elimination, to prevent the accumula- 
tion of static electricity when the beads arc shaken 
on the surface of geotextile. Commercially avail- 
able devices or *anti-static' sprays are acceptable.

6 PREPARATION OF TEST SPECIMEN 

6.1 Cut five specimens from sample of geoiextile 
wtth each specimen being cut to fit the appropriate 
sieve pan. 



IS 14294 : 1995 



6.2 Weigh the specimens and then submerge ihem 
in distilled water for 1 hour at the standard atmos- 
phere specified in IS 6359 : 1971. 

6.3 Dry the specimens and glass beads at 30°C until 
no weight (mass) change is recorded. Probable time 
required may be between 12 and 24 hours. 

7 PROCEDURE 

7J Carryout the test at the standard atmosphere 
for testing textiles in such a manner that staiic 
electricity is prevented from affecting test results. If 
standard atmosphere cannot be maintained and 
staiic electricity is observed, any of the followmg 
methods may be used to prevent static electricity. 

7.1.1 Install static eliminating dcvjccs equally 
spaced along the circumference of sieve and one on 
centre of cover, or 

7.1.2 Apply commercially available *anii-staiic' 
spray uniformly to the geoiextile. 

7.2 Secure the gcotextile between two sieves. It is 
important that the geolcxiilc be supported so that 
il IS light, without wrinkles or bulges. The gcoicxtilc 
shall not be stretched or deformed such that U chan- 
ges or distorts the opcnmgs in the fabric. Two sys- 
tems may be used to secure the geotcxiilc sample 

7.2.1 Wedge between two sieve frames. 

7.2.2 Secure with hoop inside sieve frame, 

7.3 Prior to each use, sieve the glass beads in the 
laboratory lo verify size of beads 

7.4 Starl with the smallest diameter glass beads 
that will be tested. Place 50 g of one size glass beads 
on the centre of the gcotcxiile. 

7.5 Place cover and pan on sieve frame and place 
in shaker. Shake sieves for 10 minutes. 

7.6 Place the glass beads still on the surface of the 
specimen in a pan and weigh. Include beads that fall 
off as a result of turning the specimen over and 
tapping the rims of the sieves. 

NOl'E — The sicp provides infonniuon concerning the 
amount of glass beads trapped within ihe geoiextile and the 
amount of any beads lost during testing 

7.7 Weigh the glass beads that pass through the 
specimen, and record data on a worksheet {see 
Annex A for a sample worksheet). 

7.8 Repeat 7.3 through 7,7 using the next larger 
bead size fraction. Repeat the trial using succeed- 
ingly larger bead size fractions until the weight of 
beads passing through the specimen is 5 percent or 



less. Perform the trials such that the percent pass- 
ing decreases from a value greater than 5 percent to 
a value less than or equal to 5 percent 

NOTB — All size glass beads are sieved through a single 
specimen of geoiextile, Geotexiile vanabihly would make it 
difficull lo obtain consislent results by sieving each size glass 
bead through a separate specimen 

7.9 Repeal 7.2 to 7.8 for all five specimens. 

8 CALCULATIONS 

8.1 For each size of beads tested with each 
specimen, compute to the nearest percent the beads 
passing through the specimen using the following 
equation: 

B = lOOP/T 
where 

B 

P 

T 



= beads passing through specimen, percent; 
= mass of glass beads in the pan, g, and 
= total mabs of glass beads used, g. 



8.2 Record calculations and percent beads passing 
(see Annex A). 

8.3 Assign the AOS for each specimen as the size 
designation in millimetres (see 53) of the beads of 
which 5 percent or less pass. 

8.4 Determine the AOS for the sample by averag- 
ing the AOS values of the five specimens. 

NOTE — It IS oRen desirable lo compare the data from e^ch 
specimen by ploiting the percentage beads passing ihe 
specimen versus bead size for each of the bead sizes used for 
each specimen and (o evaluate the consistency of the le&Ung 
operation for miernal qujliiy coniro] Plotting is also 
desirable when the results of two laboratories differ and ilis 
desired lo com pare the data from each laboratory to pinpoint 
ilie cause of Uie discrepancy 

9 REPORT 

Report shall include the following information: 

a) IS number of the method followed for test- 
ing; 

b) Bead size range (in millimetres) used; 

c) Plots of bead size versus percentage beads 
passing for each specimen, if required; 

d) The average apparent opening size (AOS = 
0<js) in millimetres; 

e) When requested, AOS m terms of sieve 
number, that is, having nominal openings, 
in millimetres, next larger than or equal to 
the AOS, in millimetres; and 

f) Deviation, if any.

Review of Indian Standards 

Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also 
reviewed periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that 
no changes are needed; if the review indicates thai changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users 
of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in possession of the laiest amendments or edition by 
referring to the latest issue of 'BIS Handbook' and 'Standards Monthly Additions'.
